questions.q: What did the Beginner tier's approach stop at?
options: Raw CSVs cataloged by a Glue crawler and queried ad hoc via Athena
A fully scheduled Glue ETL job writing to Redshift
A Redshift Serverless warehouse with dimension and fact tables
A nightly EventBridge-triggered refresh pipeline
questions.explain: The Beginner tier landed raw CSVs in S3, cataloged them with northfield-raw-crawler, and queried them ad hoc through Athena — nothing scheduled or transformed.

questions.q: What is Finance's actual new request, in plain terms?
options: The same regional revenue numbers every month, without anyone re-running a query by hand
A single one-time report for this quarter only
Direct read access to the raw S3 CSV files
A dashboard with no numbers, just narrative commentary
questions.explain: Finance wants a repeatable, trustworthy monthly dataset, not another one-off query someone has to remember to run.

questions.q: Why can't relying on ad hoc Athena queries as the primary path satisfy a recurring, trusted report?
options: No single place owns the transformation logic, so different analysts' queries can quietly disagree
Athena cannot run SQL queries against Glue Catalog tables
Athena deletes raw data after each query
It satisfies the request perfectly, with no real downside
questions.explain: Without a single, owned transformation step, every analyst's hand-written query can cast, dedupe, or filter slightly differently — which is exactly how two reports end up disagreeing.

questions.q: What two new AWS pieces does this chapter introduce to make the dataset repeatable?
options: A Glue ETL job (northfield-orders-etl) and a Redshift warehouse (northfield-analytics)
A second raw S3 bucket and a second Athena workgroup
Step Functions orchestration and CloudWatch monitoring
A new on-premises SQL Server instance
questions.explain: This tier adds the Glue ETL job northfield-orders-etl and the Redshift Serverless workgroup northfield-analytics; Step Functions and CloudWatch belong to the Advanced tier.

questions.q: How does this Intermediate tier relate to the existing Advanced tier (aws-capstone)?
options: The Advanced tier adds orchestration, monitoring, CI/CD, IAM hardening, and DR on top of the exact same pipeline this tier builds
The Advanced tier replaces every resource this tier creates with new names
The two tiers use entirely unrelated data and services
The Advanced tier is a prerequisite you must complete before this one
questions.explain: The Advanced tier builds on top of this tier's same northfield-orders-etl-to-Redshift pipeline, which is why none of this tier's resource names can change later.
